column1: # clues.tsv for ft_point.h — hints only, never answers.
# (Single member-less hint: this exercise's failure is one compile, not a table.)

The failure you are reading comes from compiling the subject's own main against your header. It declares a variable of type t_point and writes 42 and 21 to point->x and point->y through a pointer. Work back from that. What kind of thing must t_point be for ->x and ->y to exist at all, and what can hold those two values? Note the name: the 42 Norm has a rule about what a type you define yourself must be called and how it is introduced, and t_ is not decoration. And as with any header, what keeps it safe to #include more than once in a single build?
